failures_only: The time was predicted in milliseconds for a machine as it stood an hour before and was measured on one at a load average of 21 to 28: neither side is near its predicted number, and the three calls' ratios differ (0.674, 0.911, 0.697 of installed's milliseconds a step; 0.663 in the timed pair). The second call's kept side was itself slow (20.2 ms a step). A recorder's time moves with the machine's load by more than the difference between calls, so the gain is known as a ratio under load, not as milliseconds on a quiet machine.

During the third call's installed side another process held card 0 beside the recorder (12.7 GB on the card at its most): that call's installed 32.45 ms a step is not the recorder alone, and its ratio flatters the kept side. Without that call the two others give 21.37 and 16.95 ms a step, 0.793.

The launch calls themselves are 0.9 ms of an installed step (4.7 s over 5,250 steps), and the kept side saved 6.5 ms a step in that same pair. So the launches' host duration is not where the saving is either: it is in what the scheduler and the backend do around each of the 247 ranges (and under load, in giving the processor up 247 times a compute), which this run measures only jointly with the change of allocation. The hypothesis of recorder-deferred-original's record (about 4 ms for the 212 ranges) was the right place and the wrong size under this load.

The kept side holds more of the card: 5.6 to 6.1 GB at its most in the samples against 5.05 GB installed, since no node's memory is given to a later node. A recorder beside another job on a card needs that room.
what_this_changes: A split computed as one graph, with every node kept from reuse and the 212 wanted outputs copied to pinned host memory after it and waited for once, is the same computation as the installed stop at each output on this card, engine and model: 30 of 30 answers' files are the same bytes, and 10 of 10 again with the engine's timer on. The card's backend computes the same bytes from one graph as from 247 ranges.

It is faster wherever it was measured: 0.756 of the installed milliseconds a step over the run, 25 of 27 answers, every call. On the measured ratio a capture's generation of 204 s would be about 154 s; that is arithmetic on a ratio taken under load, and the quiet-machine time is not measured. It also removes 247 waits a compute at which the recorder gives up the processor, which is what a loaded machine makes expensive.

Using it in a capture is a separate acceptance and is proposed to Astra, not done here: own_text.py's recorder call with the kept engine folder ahead of the recorder's library folder and GGML_SCHED_EVAL_KEPT=1, the engine's identity naming both folders, and a reader protocol made again (the kept library's sha256 beside the installed engine's). No instrument, capture or protocol is changed by this run: controlled-bf16-7 and the installed engine stay.

The card is still idle much of the time on both sides (utilization in the samples: median 37 to 44 on the installed side of the undisturbed calls, 43 to 60 on the kept side), so what bounds a kept token is still on the processor side. The next variant, several recorder contexts as threads of one process, is built and declared separately (recorder-workers-original).
